raw_response:
I farm only 7 mu, so I cannot take big risks. What I do must first keep the grain steady, and second not spend too much cash at one time. I have done wheat-maize for many years, and around here everybody does it this way, so I will keep the same system. For wheat, I will sow in early October after I clear the summer field, use a common improved seed from the local dealer, and put most fertilizer at planting so I do not have to chase too many operations later. If the wheat苗 looks weak after winter, I will add some urea at jointing. Water costs money, but wheat in our place usually still needs a few irrigations, so I plan three times if the rain is normal. After wheat harvest in June, I will not waste time with heavy tillage because the maize must go in quickly. I will use the same 7 mu for summer maize right after wheat, put fertilizer once at planting and once when it grows taller, and irrigate only if the rain is not enough. I keep the plan fairly safe: not the highest input, but not too little either, because if I save too much on fertilizer and water, the yield loss hurts more.

decision.reasoning_summary: I am farming only 7 mu, and some people in my house work outside, so I must keep the work and cash use steady. I still plant wheat and maize on the same land because this is what works here and gives me grain in both seasons. I use moderate fertilizer, not too high, because inputs are expensive, but I do not dare cut too much either since low yield is a bigger problem. Wheat gets more water because it depends on irrigation more in our place, while maize mostly follows the summer rain and I add one irrigation if needed.
